references.notes: Full text read via WebFetch of the AAAAI-hosted PDF (first 100,000 of 109,883 characters; the unread tail is the reference list region). WebFetch quotes are capped near 125 characters, so long passages are quoted in part. The prior page claimed a "peak at 48 to 72 hours" and "some reactions last a week or more"; neither appears in the parameter (it gives 24 to 48 hours of growth and 3 to 10 days to resolve), so both were removed. The 4% to 10% figure for a systemic reaction after a large local reaction is from the executive summary; another passage gives about 7% (range 4% to 15%).

claims.text: Large local reaction: swelling over 10 cm contiguous with the sting that increases for 24 to 48 hours
claims.quote: Increase in size for 24 to 48 hours ... Swelling to more than 10 cm in diameter contiguous to the site of the sting

claims.text: Swelling usually increases 6 to 12 hours after the sting
claims.quote: the swelling usually increases 6 to 12 hours after the sting

claims.text: Large local swelling subsides over 3 to 10 days
claims.quote: subsides after 3 to 10 days

claims.text: Large local reaction is usually an IgE-mediated late-phase reaction
claims.quote: Marked local swelling extending from the sting site is usually an IgE-mediated late-phase reaction.

claims.text: Small local reaction: pain, swelling and redness lasting a few hours to a few days
claims.quote: characterized by pain, swelling, and redness, which usually last from a few hours to a few days

claims.text: Swelling and even lymphangitic streaks may be from mast cell mediators, not infection; not cellulitis
claims.quote: Swelling (and even lymphangitis) may be caused by mast cell mediator release and not by infection ... They do not represent cellulitis even though lymphangitic streaks may be present.

claims.text: Antibiotics not indicated unless clear evidence of secondary infection; prescribe only if specifically indicated
claims.quote: antibiotics are not indicated unless there is clear evidence of secondary infection ... Antibiotics are usually not necessary and should be prescribed only if specifically indicated.

claims.text: Symptomatic treatment of large local reactions with antihistamines, cold compresses, analgesics; short oral steroid course may be useful in severe cases; grade D evidence
claims.quote: Treat large local reactions symptomatically, with antihistamines, cold compresses, and analgesics as needed. In severe cases a short course of oral corticosteroids may be useful. ... (Recommendation; D evidence)

claims.text: Cold compresses, oral antihistamines and analgesics might help
claims.quote: Cold compresses might help to reduce local pain and swelling. ... Oral antihistamines and oral analgesics might also help to reduce the pain or itching

claims.text: Controlled-study proof that oral steroids work for large local reactions is lacking
claims.quote: Many physicians use oral corticosteroids for large local reactions, although definitive proof of efficacy through controlled studies is lacking.

claims.text: Systemic reactions are manifestations not contiguous with the sting
claims.quote: Systemic reactions can include a spectrum of manifestations not contiguous with the site of the sting

claims.text: Anaphylaxis defined as hypotension or involvement of at least 2 organ systems
claims.quote: anaphylaxis includes hypotension or involvement of at least 2 organ systems

claims.text: Treat acute systemic sting reactions like anaphylaxis with timely epinephrine and transport to an emergency department
claims.quote: Advise the patient to treat acute systemic reactions to insect stings like any anaphylactic reaction, with timely ... epinephrine injection ... and transport to an emergency department.

claims.text: Refer to an allergist after a systemic sting reaction
claims.quote: Patients who have experienced a systemic reaction to an insect sting should be referred to an allergist

claims.text: Large local reaction carries a 4% to 10% risk of a future systemic reaction
claims.quote: The risk of a systemic reaction in patients who experience large local reactions is 4% to 10%.

claims.text: About 50% risk of systemic reaction to a future sting after a prior systemic reaction
claims.quote: The frequency of systemic reaction to a future sting in patients with a history of systemic reactions to stings is approximately 50%.

claims.text: 50% of fatal sting reactions occur with the first reaction
claims.quote: One of the greatest concerns is that 50% of fatal sting reactions occur with the first reaction

claims.text: VIT generally not required for large local reactions only; might be considered with frequent unavoidable exposure
claims.quote: Counsel patients who have experienced only large local reactions to stings that VIT is generally not required ... but might be considered in those who have frequent unavoidable exposure.

claims.text: Cutaneous-only systemic reactions (children and adults): VIT generally not required, may be considered in special circumstances as a shared decision
claims.quote: advise both children and adults who have experienced only cutaneous systemic reactions ... that VIT is generally not required but may be considered when there are special circumstances. This should be a shared decision

claims.text: Recommend VIT after an anaphylactic sting reaction with venom-specific IgE
claims.quote: Recommend and initiate VIT in all patients who have experienced an anaphylactic reaction to an insect sting and who have specific IgE to venom allergens

claims.text: Do not start VIT on testing alone without a systemic reaction history
claims.quote: Avoid VIT based solely on in vivo and in vitro testing for venom IgE, without a history of systemic reaction to a sting.

claims.text: Venom IgE in more than 20% of healthy adults; only 5% to 15% react; testing cannot screen asymptomatic people
claims.quote: Positive serum or skin test results for venom IgE are present in more than 20% of healthy adults ... only 5% to 15% ... For this reason, venom testing cannot be used to screen asymptomatic children or adults.

claims.text: Local swelling in the oropharynx can compromise the airway
claims.quote: could cause airway compromise if the sting occurs in the oropharynx (eg, after drinking from a straw or canned beverage).

claims.text: Honeybees usually leave a barbed stinger and venom sac; ground-nesting yellow jackets can also leave stingers
claims.quote: Honeybees usually leave a barbed stinger and attached venom sac in the skin after they sting ... Other insects, particularly ground-nesting yellow jackets, also can leave stingers in the skin.

claims.text: Honeybees usually nonaggressive away from hives except Africanized; yellow jackets very aggressive
claims.quote: Honeybees, except for Africanized honeybees, are usually nonaggressive away from their hives. ... Yellow jackets are very aggressive and sting with minimum provocation.

claims.text: Multiple stings make systemic reactions more likely; unusual delayed, mostly toxic reactions incl. renal failure with rhabdomyolysis
claims.quote: Systemic reactions may be more likely in response to multiple stings or sequential stings ... renal failure (with rhabdomyolysis). These reactions are mostly toxic in nature and delayed in onset

claims.text: Avoidance: nests removed by trained professionals; caution eating or drinking outdoors; avoid barefoot or sandals
claims.quote: have known or suspected nests in the immediate vicinity of the patient's home removed by trained professionals ... avoid eating or drinking outdoors ... avoid walking outside barefoot or with open shoes (sandals)

claims.text: Carry an epinephrine autoinjector; consider medical identification
claims.quote: the need to always carry an epinephrine autoinjector ... Patients should also consider obtaining and carrying a medical identification bracelet or necklace.

claims.text: Patients should be prescribed and instructed in use of injectable epinephrine
claims.quote: should be given a prescription for an injectable epinephrine device, be instructed in its proper use

claims.text: Future risk and carrying epinephrine after strictly cutaneous systemic reactions is individualized (low-risk group)
claims.quote: those with a history of only large local reactions to stings or of strictly cutaneous systemic reactions
